items.q: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre un hábito y una racha?
items.a: Una racha cuenta cuánto tiempo ha continuado algo desde una fecha de inicio o un reinicio. Un hábito te pide completar algo según un horario: diario, varias veces al día, semanal, mensual o personalizado. Ambos viven en Since.

meta.title: How Account and Sync Work in Left | Left
meta.description: Sign in with Apple in Left to back up your dates, habits, streaks, and friends, and sync across devices.

account_and_sync.p_1: Left can be used locally, but an account is what lets your important data follow you beyond one device. When you sign in with Apple, Left creates an account-backed profile and can save your main app data in the cloud so it can appear again when you sign in on another iPhone or iPad. Sync is automatic, but timing depends on the network, cloud service availability, and whether the previous device finished syncing.
account_and_sync.p_extra_1: You can create an account when you open Left for the first time, or later from Settings → Account → Sign in.
account_and_sync.p_2: Left uses Sign in with Apple. After signing in, your account can store your profile and cloud-backed app data so it can appear on other devices where you sign in with the same account.
account_and_sync.p_3: When you are signed in, Left saves account-backed data in the cloud, including:
account_and_sync.li_2: Your profile photo or profile symbol.
account_and_sync.li_5: Shared friend data such as Joint Ahead dates and shared Since invitations.
account_and_sync.p_4: Once the data is in the cloud, signing in on another device should bring it across automatically. Sync timing can vary depending on network connection, cloud service availability, and whether the app has had time to finish syncing.
account_and_sync.p_5: Some preferences are device-specific and may not follow your account.
account_and_sync.p_6: For example, app appearance choices, local display preferences, selected layouts, and other device-level settings can remain on the device where you set them. If something looks different on a second device, check the relevant Settings section and adjust it there.
account_and_sync.h2_4: How to sign in on another device
account_and_sync.p_7: On the other iPhone or iPad:
account_and_sync.li_extra_1: Sign in with the same Apple account, either during first launch or from Settings → Account → Sign in.
account_and_sync.li_10: Keep the app open for a moment so cloud data can load.
account_and_sync.p_8: Your account data should appear after sync completes. If you delete the app but already had an account, signing in again should normally restore your cloud-backed data, but this cannot be guaranteed in every situation because cloud sync depends on service availability and the previous data having synced successfully.
account_and_sync.p_extra_2: Go to Settings → Account to manage your account.
account_and_sync.li_12: Choose a profile photo or profile symbol.
account_and_sync.p_10: Your username is unique and lets other Left users find you. It uses lowercase letters and numbers.
account_and_sync.p_extra_3: Delete account removes your Left account and related cloud data from Left's systems. It can take time for deletion to complete across all systems.
account_and_sync.p_11: Deleting your account does not remove data that is already stored locally on the device. If you want to remove local app data too, delete the app from the device after deleting the account.
account_and_sync.p_extra_4: If you only want to stop using account sync temporarily, use Sign out instead of deleting the account.
account_and_sync.p_12: Download Left on your iPhone to see the time you have left, dates you are looking forward to, build the habits you want to keep, and become a better version of yourself.

meta.title: How to Be Accountable to Friends in Left | Left
meta.description: Invite a friend to watch a specific habit or streak in Left for lightweight accountability.

accountability_with_friends.h1_1: How to be accountable to friends
accountability_with_friends.p_1: Habits and streaks are easier to keep when someone else knows they matter to you. Left's accountability features stay private and intentional: you choose the exact habit or streak, you choose the friend, and they only see what you invited them to watch. It is different from posting progress publicly — the friend becomes a watcher for one selected Since item.
accountability_with_friends.p_2: You choose a specific streak or habit and invite a friend to watch it. If they accept, they become a watcher for that item.
accountability_with_friends.p_3: This is private by default. Friends do not automatically see all your habits, all your streaks, or the other friends you invited. They only see the shared item you selected.
accountability_with_friends.p_4: Before you can ask someone to keep you accountable, they need to be your friend on Left.
accountability_with_friends.p_extra_1: Open Friends, tap +, and either share Your invite link or search for them with Search by @username. Once the request is accepted, you can share individual habits and streaks with them.
accountability_with_friends.h2_3: Step 2 — Share a habit or streak
accountability_with_friends.p_5: You can share when creating or editing a habit or streak.
accountability_with_friends.li_1: Create a new habit or streak, or open an existing one.
accountability_with_friends.li_2: Choose the friend you want to invite.
accountability_with_friends.p_extra_2: Friends you invite may appear as Invited until they accept. Once accepted, they appear as Watching.
accountability_with_friends.h2_4: Step 3 — What your friend can see
accountability_with_friends.p_6: When a friend accepts the invite, they can see that shared streak or habit and its progress.
accountability_with_friends.p_7: For habits, they can see whether you complete or miss the habit. For streaks, they can see whether the streak is still going or has restarted. From the shared detail screen, they can send support or congratulations when the app allows it.
accountability_with_friends.p_8: This makes accountability lightweight: your friend can encourage you before a habit is complete, or send congratulations after you complete it.
accountability_with_friends.p_9: You can stop sharing at any time.
accountability_with_friends.p_extra_3: Open the shared habit or streak, go to the Friends section, and remove the friend from the item. If you are watching someone else's item, you can leave it from the shared item details.
accountability_with_friends.p_10: Removing sharing stops that person from watching the item going forward.
accountability_with_friends.p_extra_4: Go to Settings → Friends to choose what can notify you:
accountability_with_friends.p_12: Your friend can choose their own notification settings too. They may decide to get alerts when you complete or miss shared Since activity, or turn those notifications off.
accountability_with_friends.p_13: Download Left on your iPhone to see the time you have left, dates you are looking forward to, build the habits you want to keep, and become a better version of yourself.

meta.title: How to Add Friends on Left | Left
meta.description: Sign in, share your invite link or search by username, and accept friend requests in Left.

add_friends.h1_1: How to add friends on Left
add_friends.p_1: Friends is the social layer in Left. It is not a public profile network and it does not make all your data visible. It exists so you can intentionally share selected parts of Left with people you trust. Adding a friend is only the first step — a friend does not automatically see all your Ahead dates, habits, or streaks. Individual items are shared later, one by one.
add_friends.p_extra_1: If you are not signed in, open Friends and tap Sign in with Apple. You can also go to Settings → Account and tap Sign in.
add_friends.p_3: Signing in gives you a profile and a unique username so other Left users can find you.
add_friends.p_extra_2: Open the Friends section in Left. If you are signed in, you will see your friends list and a + button.
add_friends.p_extra_3: Tap the + button to open Add a Friend.
add_friends.p_extra_4: In Add a Friend, Left shows Your invite link.
add_friends.li_2: Share it with the share button.
add_friends.li_3: Send it to someone in Messages, Mail, or any app you use.
add_friends.p_5: When someone opens your invite link, they can send or accept the friend invite from Left.
add_friends.p_6: You can also add someone directly by username.
add_friends.li_extra_2: If Left finds the profile, tap Invite.
add_friends.p_extra_5: If they already sent you a request, you may see Accept instead. If you already sent a request, the row will show Pending.
add_friends.p_extra_6: Incoming friend requests appear in Friend Requests.
add_friends.li_5: If there are pending friend requests, tap the person badge button at the top.
add_friends.li_extra_4: In Friend Requests, use the Requests tab to accept or decline incoming requests.
add_friends.li_extra_5: Use the Pending tab to see requests you have sent.
add_friends.p_extra_7: Shared invitations are separate. If someone invites you to watch a streak or habit, or to join a Joint Ahead date, a bell badge appears at the top of Friends. Tap it to open Requests, where shared items are grouped under Shared streaks and habits and Joint Ahead dates.
add_friends.p_7: After someone accepts your friend request, you can:
add_friends.li_6: Invite them to Joint Ahead dates.
add_friends.li_7: Ask them to watch individual habits or streaks.
add_friends.li_8: Let them see selected progress and send encouragement.
add_friends.li_9: See shared dates, habits, and streaks from that friend when they choose to share them with you.
add_friends.p_8: Friendship alone does not make everything public. Ahead dates, habits, and streaks are shared only when you choose the item and invite that friend.
add_friends.p_9: Download Left on your iPhone to see the time you have left, dates you are looking forward to, build the habits you want to keep, and become a better version of yourself.

meta.title: How to Choose Your Tools in Left | Left
meta.description: Pick which Left tools appear in the bottom menu, set their order, choose a default, and hide names.

choose_your_tools.p_1: Left has more tools than can comfortably fit in the main bottom menu at once. Choose your tools lets you decide which tools deserve the fastest access — pick what appears in the bottom menu, set the order, choose which one opens by default, and decide whether the menu shows names or just icons. Everything else stays inside the tools button at the end of the bottom menu.
choose_your_tools.h2_1: What the bottom menu is for
choose_your_tools.p_2: The bottom menu is the fastest way to move around Left. It is meant for the tools you use most often, not necessarily every tool in the app.
choose_your_tools.p_extra_1: You can display between 2 and 4 tools in the main menu. This keeps the menu usable and prevents it from becoming crowded. The default setup starts with core tools such as Time Left, Time Ahead, and Time Since, but you can change that to match how you actually use Left.
choose_your_tools.li_1: Look at the preview at the top of the screen.
choose_your_tools.p_5: The preview shows how the bottom menu will look with your current choices. As you select, remove, reorder, or hide names, the preview helps you understand the layout before you leave Settings.
choose_your_tools.h2_3: Step 2 — Choose the tools to pin
choose_your_tools.p_6: In the tool list, tap a tool to select or deselect it.
choose_your_tools.p_7: Left lets you choose between 2 and 4 tools for the main menu. If you already have 4 selected, you need to remove one before adding another. If you only have 2 selected, Left keeps those selected so the menu does not become too empty.
choose_your_tools.p_8: Choose the tools you want to reach quickly. A good setup is usually based on your daily behaviour:
choose_your_tools.li_extra_12: Pick Time Left if you use Left mainly as a time awareness app.
choose_your_tools.li_extra_13: Pick Time Ahead if countdown dates are important to you.
choose_your_tools.li_extra_14: Pick Time Since if streaks and habits are part of your routine.
choose_your_tools.li_extra_15: Pick Planner if you use Left to understand your day.
choose_your_tools.li_extra_16: Pick Friends if accountability and shared dates matter to you.
choose_your_tools.li_extra_17: Pick You if you often check your profile, lifespan, and personal reflections.
choose_your_tools.p_9: There is no correct setup. The best menu is the one that removes friction from the parts of Left you actually use.
choose_your_tools.h2_4: Step 3 — Choose what opens by default
choose_your_tools.p_extra_2: Use Open app by default in... to choose the tool Left should open first.
choose_your_tools.p_10: Only selected tools appear in this picker. If you want a tool to be the default, make sure it is selected in the main tool list first.
choose_your_tools.p_extra_3: For example, if you want Left to always open on Planner, select Planner as one of your tools, then choose it in Open app by default in.... If you later remove that tool from the menu, Left will choose another selected tool as the default.
choose_your_tools.p_11: The order of selected tools controls how they appear in the bottom menu.
choose_your_tools.li_2: Drag the selected tools into the order you want.
choose_your_tools.p_extra_4: The footer changes to Drag to change the order. Selected tools keep that order in the main menu. while you are reordering. Only the selected tools are shown in this mode, so you can focus on the tools that will actually appear in the bottom menu.
choose_your_tools.h2_6: Step 5 — Hide tool names if you prefer icons
choose_your_tools.p_extra_5: Turn on Hide names if you want a cleaner bottom menu with icons only.
choose_your_tools.p_13: This is useful if you already know the icons or prefer a more minimal layout. If you want the menu to be easier to read at a glance, leave names visible.
choose_your_tools.p_14: You can switch this setting back at any time.
choose_your_tools.h2_7: Where the rest of the tools go
choose_your_tools.p_15: Tools that are not selected do not disappear. They move behind the tools button at the end of the bottom menu.
choose_your_tools.p_16: That button uses the tools icon and always remains available. Tap it when you want to open a tool that is not pinned in your main menu. This is the balance Left is aiming for: your favourite tools stay one tap away, and everything else remains accessible without crowding the interface.
choose_your_tools.p_extra_6: Changes save automatically when you leave Choose your tools.
choose_your_tools.p_17: Download Left on your iPhone to see the time you have left, dates you are looking forward to, build the habits you want to keep, and become a better version of yourself.

meta.title: How Joint Ahead Dates Work in Left | Left

joint_ahead_dates.p_1: Ahead is for dates you are looking forward to: trips, birthdays, deadlines, events, and anything else that gives the future a shape. A Joint Ahead date is an Ahead date shared with friends. You create the date, invite one or more friends, and they can accept the invitation so the date appears for them too. The creator stays the admin; accepted participants keep the same countdown in their own Left.
joint_ahead_dates.h2_1: What is a Joint Ahead date?
joint_ahead_dates.p_2: A Joint Ahead date is an Ahead date shared with friends. The creator is the admin. The admin can edit the main details and manage who is invited. Accepted friends also get the date in their Ahead view.
joint_ahead_dates.p_3: Multiple friends can join the same Joint Ahead date, so everyone can count down to the same plan.
joint_ahead_dates.p_4: Joint Ahead works with friends, so add the people first.
joint_ahead_dates.p_extra_1: Open Friends, tap +, and either share Your invite link or use Search by @username. Once someone accepts, you can invite them to an Ahead date.
joint_ahead_dates.h2_3: Step 2 — Create or open an Ahead date
joint_ahead_dates.li_1: Open an existing Ahead date and edit it.
joint_ahead_dates.p_6: When creating or editing the date:
joint_ahead_dates.p_extra_3: Friends you invite may appear as Invited until they accept. The creator appears as Creator, accepted participants can appear as Friend, and your own row can appear as You.
joint_ahead_dates.p_extra_4: When someone receives a Joint Ahead invite, a bell badge can appear in Friends. Tapping it opens Requests.
joint_ahead_dates.p_extra_5: Joint date invitations appear under Joint Ahead dates. The invited friend can accept with the checkmark or decline with the xmark.
joint_ahead_dates.p_7: After accepting, the date appears for them too. They can open it from Ahead or from the friend's shared profile area.
joint_ahead_dates.p_8: The creator/admin can update the date details, add more friends, remove pending invites, or remove participants.
joint_ahead_dates.p_extra_6: If you joined a date created by someone else, you can leave it with Leave date. Leaving removes it from your shared dates. It does not delete the date for the creator or other participants.
joint_ahead_dates.p_9: Joint Ahead is best for dates that belong to a group: a holiday, a concert, a shared launch, a wedding, or anything everyone wants to keep in view.

organise_ahead_since.p_1: Left can sort your items automatically, but automatic sorting is not always how people think about their own lives. The closest date is not always the most important date. The longest streak is not always the one you want to see first. Ahead lets you reorder dates you are looking forward to. Since lets you reorder streaks and habits. organise_ahead_since.p_2: Open the section you want to organise:
organise_ahead_since.li_extra_1: Use Ahead for dates you are counting down to.
organise_ahead_since.p_3: The same idea works in both places.
organise_ahead_since.p_extra_1: Long press an item, then tap Reorganise items.
organise_ahead_since.p_extra_2: You can do this from an Ahead date card, a streak card, or a habit card. Left enters reorganise mode and shows Cancel and Confirm at the top.
organise_ahead_since.p_4: Drag and drop the items into the order you want.
organise_ahead_since.p_5: You can move items in grid, list, or card layouts. Keep dragging until the order matches how you want the section to appear.
organise_ahead_since.p_extra_4: If you change your mind, tap Cancel instead. Cancelling leaves the previous order unchanged.
organise_ahead_since.p_extra_5: Left can sort items in several ways. In Since, sort options include Newest, Oldest, A to Z, Z to A, Longest streak, Shortest streak, and Manual. In Ahead, sort options include Closest, Farthest, A to Z, Z to A, and Manual.
organise_ahead_since.p_extra_6: Your custom order is visible when sorting is set to Manual. When you tap Confirm after reorganising, Left switches the section to Manual automatically. If you later choose another sort order, the app will show that sort instead of your custom order.

meta.title: How to Restore Purchases in Left | Left
meta.description: Reconnect a previous Left purchase via the App Store, from the purchase screen or Settings.

restore_purchases.p_1: Restoring purchases means asking the App Store to check whether your App Store account already has an active Left purchase. It is not buying again. It is a way to reconnect a previous purchase to the app when Left does not immediately detect it — useful after reinstalling, switching devices, or restoring from a backup.
restore_purchases.p_2: Purchases are connected to your App Store account. Left checks that purchase information and then updates what is available inside the app.
restore_purchases.p_extra_1: When you tap Restore purchases, Left asks the App Store for your existing purchase history and refreshes the app. If the App Store says you have an active purchase, Left applies it again. If the App Store does not return an active purchase, Left will show that nothing was found.
restore_purchases.p_3: Restoring is safe to try. It checks for an existing purchase; it does not ask you to pay again.
restore_purchases.p_4: If you see a Left purchase screen:
restore_purchases.li_1: Scroll to the bottom of the screen.
restore_purchases.li_2: Tap the restore button in the footer.
restore_purchases.li_3: Wait for Left to check your App Store purchase history.
restore_purchases.p_5: If an active purchase is found, Left applies it. If nothing is found, Left will show a message saying no active purchase was detected.
restore_purchases.p_6: You can also restore purchases from Settings.
restore_purchases.p_7: This is useful if you already closed the purchase screen or want to retry later.
restore_purchases.h2_4: Why manual restore can be needed
restore_purchases.p_8: Left refreshes purchase status automatically when the app opens and when it returns to the foreground. Most of the time, you do not need to do anything.
restore_purchases.p_extra_2: Sometimes Apple's purchase servers or the purchase service do not return the purchase immediately. This can happen after reinstalling the app, changing devices, restoring from a backup, or opening the app with a poor network connection. In those cases, tapping Restore purchases manually asks the App Store to check again.
restore_purchases.li_5: Make sure you are using the same App Store account that made the purchase.
restore_purchases.li_6: Check your internet connection and try again.
restore_purchases.li_extra_4: If restore says no purchase was found but you believe that is wrong, wait a few minutes and retry from Settings → Troubleshooting → Restore purchases.
restore_purchases.li_7: If the problem continues, contact support with the purchase receipt details available in your App Store purchase history.

set_up_your_lifespan.h1_1: How to set up your lifespan
set_up_your_lifespan.p_1: Your lifespan is one of the most important personal settings in Left. It affects how the app shows your life left, how your profile feels, and how reflective views inside Left understand your age and time remaining. Left does not treat lifespan as an exact prediction — it is an estimate used to make time visible.
set_up_your_lifespan.p_2: Left uses your lifespan setting anywhere the app needs to understand your life as a timeline.
set_up_your_lifespan.li_3: Life stages and personal reflection charts.
set_up_your_lifespan.li_4: Sleep, awake, activity, and relationship-style lifespan views.
set_up_your_lifespan.p_4: If your birthday or lifespan is missing, some of those views cannot be personalised properly. Once they are set, Left can show your life in years, months, or weeks and calculate how much of that timeline has already passed.
set_up_your_lifespan.p_extra_1: This opens the lifespan settings screen. The title at the top is Your lifespan.
set_up_your_lifespan.p_6: Your birthday tells Left where your personal timeline starts. Without it, Left cannot calculate your current age or show life progress accurately.
set_up_your_lifespan.p_extra_3: The birthday picker only allows dates up to today. Choose your actual birthday if you want the most accurate reflections in Time Left, widgets, and the You screen.
set_up_your_lifespan.h2_4: Step 3 — Choose how to see your life
set_up_your_lifespan.p_extra_4: Use See your life in... to choose how the life view is displayed.
set_up_your_lifespan.p_extra_5: Years gives the simplest view. Months makes the timeline feel more detailed. Weeks makes life feel more granular and can be more confronting because it shows many more individual units.
set_up_your_lifespan.p_extra_6: You can also turn on Hide Life in Left view if you do not want the life view to appear inside the main Time Left view. This does not delete your lifespan settings. It only hides that life section from the Left view.
set_up_your_lifespan.p_extra_7: Tap Calculate your lifespan to open the lifespan calculator.
set_up_your_lifespan.p_8: The calculator asks for broad factors that can influence life expectancy, including:
set_up_your_lifespan.p_9: Left uses these factors together to estimate a lifespan. It does not simply add or subtract a fixed number of years for each answer, and the app should not be read like a medical assessment. It is a general estimate based on the information you provide and broad statistical patterns.
set_up_your_lifespan.p_extra_8: At the top, Left shows Your life expectancy is followed by an approximate number of years. When available, you can use the Calculate button to generate an estimate from the selected factors.
set_up_your_lifespan.p_extra_9: If you do not want Left to estimate your lifespan from factors, you can choose Set your lifespan manually.
set_up_your_lifespan.p_10: Manual lifespan means you choose the number yourself instead of letting Left calculate it. This can be useful if you already have a number you want to use, if you prefer a symbolic lifespan, or if you want the app's life views to match a personal belief rather than a statistical estimate.
set_up_your_lifespan.p_11: Manual lifespan changes the number directly, so use it intentionally. It will affect how Left scales your life views, widgets, profile reflections, and time-left calculations.
set_up_your_lifespan.p_12: Your lifespan in Left is an approximation. It is meant for visual reflection, not medical advice, financial planning, or a guarantee about the future.
set_up_your_lifespan.p_13: Changing your lifespan changes how life-based views are scaled. If you increase or decrease the lifespan value, your life progress, years left, months left, weeks left, widgets, and profile reflections may change.
set_up_your_lifespan.p_14: The setting is personal. Use a number that makes Left useful for you: realistic enough to make the app meaningful, but not something you treat as a certainty.

meta.title: Streaks vs Habits in Left | Left
meta.description: How streaks and habits differ in Left, and when to choose each one.

streaks_vs_habits.p_1: Since is the part of Left for tracking time that has already started. It is where you keep the streaks you want to protect, the habits you want to build, and the counters that remind you how long something meaningful has been part of your life. Both are about consistency over time, but a streak counts automatically while a habit requires you to complete it on the schedule you chose.
streaks_vs_habits.p_2: A streak tracks time since a starting point or since the last reset. It keeps increasing automatically until you reset it.
streaks_vs_habits.p_3: Use a streak for something that does not need a daily tap from you. For example:
streaks_vs_habits.li_2: Days since you started a relationship.
streaks_vs_habits.li_3: Days since you moved to a new city.
streaks_vs_habits.li_4: Days since you began a personal challenge.
streaks_vs_habits.p_4: The key idea is that the counter keeps running by itself. If the streak ends, you restart or reset the counter.
streaks_vs_habits.p_5: A habit tracks repeated actions that you need to complete. You choose how often the habit should happen, then mark it complete when you do it.
streaks_vs_habits.p_6: Habits can be daily, weekly, monthly, or scheduled for specific days. Some habits can also require more than one completion in the same period. For example:
streaks_vs_habits.li_6: Go to the gym 3 days per week.
streaks_vs_habits.p_7: If you do not complete the habit when it is due, the habit streak can break.
streaks_vs_habits.h2_3: How they live together in Since
streaks_vs_habits.p_extra_1: Open Since and tap the + button. You can choose either Add a streak or Add an habit.
streaks_vs_habits.p_extra_2: Both streaks and habits appear in the same Since area because both are about time and consistency. You can also filter the view by All counters, Streaks, Habits, Today, or Friends, depending on what you want to focus on.
streaks_vs_habits.p_8: Templates are available for both types, so you do not always need to start from a blank item. Streak templates are useful for meaningful life counters. Habit templates are useful for routines with schedules, reminders, and completion goals.
streaks_vs_habits.p_9: Choose a streak when the thing should continue automatically unless you reset it. A streak is best for "how long since..." tracking.
streaks_vs_habits.p_10: Choose a habit when you need to take action and mark it complete. A habit is best for routines where Left should know whether you did the work today, this week, or this month.
streaks_vs_habits.p_11: For example, "days without alcohol" works well as a streak because it keeps counting until you restart it. "Go for a run" works better as a habit because you need to complete it on the days you planned.
streaks_vs_habits.p_12: Some features are specific to habits because habits have completion data:
streaks_vs_habits.li_9: Habit strength insights show how consistent the habit has become.
streaks_vs_habits.li_10: Habit schedules control when the habit is expected.
streaks_vs_habits.li_11: Multiple completions can be tracked when a habit needs to be done more than once.

wallpaper_shortcut.og_title: Cómo configurar el atajo de Left Wallpaper
wallpaper_shortcut.og_description: Crea un atajo y una automatización diaria para que el fondo de tu pantalla bloqueada se actualice solo cada día.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_1: En Atajos, toca el botón + en la esquina superior derecha para crear un nuevo atajo.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_2: En la barra de búsqueda de acciones, escribe «Left wallpaper» y toca la acción para añadirla. Esta es la acción que le pide a Left que genere un fondo de pantalla nuevo.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_3: Busca de nuevo «Establecer foto de fondo» y añade también esa acción.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_4: En la acción Establecer foto de fondo, ajusta el destino a Pantalla bloqueada.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_5: Desactiva Mostrar vista previa para que el atajo no te interrumpa cuando se ejecute.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_6: Desactiva Recortar al sujeto para que el fondo no se recorte automáticamente a una persona u objeto.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_7: Toca el nombre del atajo en la parte superior, renómbralo a algo que recuerdes como «Left Wallpaper» y toca Listo.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_8: En Atajos, cambia a la pestaña Automatización en la parte inferior.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_9: Toca el botón + y elige Hora del día como disparador.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_10: Pon la hora a las 00:01 (un minuto después de medianoche) o cualquier otra hora que prefieras.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_12: Asegúrate de que Ejecutar de inmediato está seleccionado y desactiva Notificar al ejecutarse para no recibir una notificación todos los días.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_14: En la siguiente pantalla, busca el atajo que creaste en el paso 2 (por ejemplo, «Left Wallpaper») y selecciónalo.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_16: El fondo de pantalla no se actualiza. A veces iOS retrasa las automatizaciones en segundo plano cuando el teléfono está caliente, en modo de bajo consumo o no se ha desbloqueado hace tiempo. Desbloquéalo y la automatización se pondrá al día.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_17: «Ejecutar de inmediato» está en gris. Actualiza a la última versión de iOS: las versiones anteriores requerían un toque para confirmar. iOS 17 y posteriores admiten automatizaciones totalmente desatendidas.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_18: El atajo me pide permiso cada vez. Abre Ajustes → Atajos y desactiva «Mostrar al ejecutarse» si está activado. Comprueba también que la acción de Left está en tu lista de acciones de atajos de confianza.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_19: Quiero que se actualice más de una vez al día. Crea una segunda automatización a otra hora distinta apuntando al mismo atajo. iOS aún no admite disparadores de «Hora del día» con periodicidad inferior a un día de forma nativa, pero puedes apilar dos o tres.
wallpaper_shortcut.p_extra_20: Desde dentro de la app Left, toca Abrir Atajos para saltar a la app Atajos. Luego:
wallpaper_shortcut.p_extra_21: Para mayor seguridad, añade un widget pequeño de Left a tu pantalla bloqueada junto al fondo de pantalla. Los widgets se refrescan más a menudo que los fondos, así que siempre tendrás un número actual aunque el fondo lleve unas horas de retraso. widget_mac_desktop.p_3: Descarga Left en tu iPhone para ver el tiempo que te queda, las fechas que esperas con ganas, construir los hábitos que quieres mantener y convertirte en una mejor versión de ti.

widget_mac_desktop.li_3: Pulsa Esc o haz clic en otro sitio para guardar.
widget_mac_desktop.li_4: Pincha y arrastra un widget del escritorio para colocarlo en cualquier parte.
widget_mac_desktop.li_5: Los widgets de escritorio en macOS Sonoma están disponibles en tamaños pequeño y mediano: quítalos y vuelve a añadirlos para cambiar el tamaño.
widget_mac_desktop.li_6: Los widgets quedan detrás de las ventanas de las apps y se ven al mostrar el escritorio (desliza con cuatro dedos hacia arriba y hacia los lados en el trackpad, o pulsa Mission Control).

meta.title: How to Make Left Widgets Transparent | Left
meta.description: Use the iOS Clear Home Screen style to make Left widgets blend with your wallpaper.

widget_transparent_iphone.h1_1: How to make Left widgets transparent
widget_transparent_iphone.p_1: Left is designed to live outside the app as much as inside it. The Home Screen, Lock Screen, and StandBy widgets let you keep your time left, upcoming dates, habits, and streaks visible without opening Left every time you want to check them. On iPhone, widget transparency is controlled by iOS, not by a setting inside Left — so the flow is: add the Left widget, enter Home Screen editing mode, then switch the widget appearance to Clear.
widget_transparent_iphone.p_2: Start by adding the Left widget you want to use.
widget_transparent_iphone.li_1: Long press an empty area of your iPhone Home Screen.
widget_transparent_iphone.li_2: Choose the widget you want and add it to your Home Screen.
widget_transparent_iphone.li_3: Place it where you want it to appear.
widget_transparent_iphone.p_3: The transparent style is controlled by iOS, so the widget needs to be on the Home Screen before you customize its appearance.
widget_transparent_iphone.p_4: Once the widget is on your Home Screen:
widget_transparent_iphone.li_4: Long press the Home Screen again.
widget_transparent_iphone.li_5: Wait until the apps and widgets start moving.
widget_transparent_iphone.li_6: Stay on this screen. This is the same mode you use to move or remove apps and widgets.
widget_transparent_iphone.p_5: At the top of the screen:
widget_transparent_iphone.li_7: Tap outside the customization panel or finish editing when you are done.
widget_transparent_iphone.p_6: Your Left widgets should now use the clear Home Screen style, so they sit more naturally over your wallpaper.
widget_transparent_iphone.li_extra_6: I do not see Clear. Make sure your iPhone is updated to a version of iOS that supports clear widget styling.
widget_transparent_iphone.li_extra_7: The widget still has a background. Remove the widget and add it again, then repeat Edit → Customize → Clear.
widget_transparent_iphone.li_8: Only some widgets changed. The clear option is an iOS Home Screen appearance setting. Check that you are customizing the correct Home Screen page and widget style.
widget_transparent_iphone.p_7: Download Left on your iPhone to see the time you have left, dates you are looking forward to, build the habits you want to keep, and become a better version of yourself.

meta.description: Consigue ayuda con Left: widgets de tiempo restante, hábitos, rachas, cuentas atrás, Planner, sincronización, Left Premium y más.

support.p_1: ¿Tienes problemas con Left? Preguntas comunes, resolución de problemas y cómo conseguir más ayuda.
support.p_2: Guías paso a paso para añadir widgets de Left en todas las plataformas de Apple.
support.p_3: Widgets pequeños, medianos y grandes, configurados en segundos.
support.p_4: Ve tu cuenta atrás sin desbloquear. Requiere iOS 16 o posterior.
support.p_5: Convierte tu iPhone cargando en una pantalla de cuenta atrás de mesilla.
support.p_6: Incluye el tamaño extra grande exclusivo del iPad.
support.p_7: Cuentas atrás de un vistazo en tu iPad. Requiere iPadOS 16 o posterior.
support.p_8: Un clic en el reloj y tu cuenta atrás está ahí.
support.p_9: Widgets siempre a la vista en el escritorio. macOS Sonoma o posterior.
support.p_10: Cuenta atrás del trabajo en la oficina, cuenta atrás de vacaciones en casa, automáticamente.
support.p_11: Cambia lo que muestra un widget, muévelo o quítalo del todo.
support.p_12: Una pulsación para ver tu cuenta atrás, mediante Atajos. iPhone 15 Pro o posterior.
support.p_13: Automatiza Left: ábrelo con Siri, con el botón Acción o con disparadores por hora.
support.p_14: Haz que tu pantalla bloqueada se actualice sola cada día con datos de tiempo en directo.
support.p_15: Sí. Time Left, más de 20 widgets, You, Wallpaper, Friends, Time Between, juegos y otras herramientas básicas son gratis para siempre.
support.p_16: Left calcula el tiempo desde el momento actual hasta la fecha objetivo en tu zona horaria local. La cuenta atrás se actualiza cada vez que se refresca el widget, normalmente cada 15-30 minutos, con un refresco inmediato cuando abres la app.
support.p_17: Sí. Al editar un widget (mantén pulsado → Editar widget), puedes elegir el estilo de presentación: solo días, días y horas, desglose completo o porcentaje. Las opciones disponibles dependen del tamaño del widget.
support.p_18: La vista de porcentaje muestra cuánto ha pasado de un periodo de tiempo. Por ejemplo, si estás siguiendo el año, muestra qué porcentaje del año ha pasado. Para un evento con cuenta atrás, muestra cuánto ha pasado del tiempo entre la creación y la fecha objetivo.
support.p_19: iOS gestiona el presupuesto de actualizaciones de los widgets para cuidar la batería. Abrir Left refresca todos los widgets de inmediato. Si no, el sistema programa refrescos aproximadamente cada 15-30 minutos. Es una limitación de iOS que afecta a todas las apps.
support.p_20: Abre la app Left una vez para forzar un refresco. Si el widget sigue mostrando una fecha antigua, quítalo y vuelve a añadirlo: eso reinicia la conexión de datos del widget con Left.
support.p_21: iOS no permite que los widgets de la pantalla de inicio muestren los segundos en directo: solo pueden actualizarse cada cierto tiempo. Los widgets de la pantalla bloqueada también tienen este límite. Para una cuenta atrás segundo a segundo, abre la app Left directamente.
support.p_22: Time Left, más de 20 widgets, You, Wallpaper, Friends, Time Between, juegos y otras herramientas básicas son gratis para siempre. Left Premium desbloquea formas más profundas de seguir hábitos, rachas, fechas especiales y tu día.
support.p_23: Sí. Left Premium está vinculado a tu Apple ID, no a un único dispositivo. En cualquier dispositivo con la sesión iniciada en el mismo Apple ID, toca «Restaurar compras» en los ajustes de Left para desbloquear las funciones Premium.
support.p_24: Las compras de por vida pueden ser compatibles con En Familia según los ajustes de compra de Apple. Asegúrate de que En Familia está activado en los ajustes de tu Apple ID y de que «Compartir compras» está activado para tu grupo familiar.
support.p_25: Inicia sesión con el mismo Apple ID y cuenta de iCloud en tu nuevo dispositivo y luego instala Left. Al abrirla por primera vez, Left sincronizará tus eventos y hábitos desde iCloud automáticamente. Puede tardar un poco según la velocidad de tu conexión.
support.p_26: Tus eventos se guardan en iCloud si la sincronización está activada, lo que funciona como copia de seguridad automática en todos tus dispositivos. De momento no hay exportación manual. Si la sincronización con iCloud está desactivada, los datos viven solo en tu dispositivo.
support.p_27: Sí. Left funciona en el dispositivo sin iCloud. Puedes usar la app principal sin sincronización entre dispositivos. Las funciones compartidas usan tu cuenta gratuita de Left, e iCloud hace falta para la sincronización automática entre dispositivos de Apple.
support.p_28: No. Left no tiene procesos persistentes en segundo plano. iOS dibuja los widgets según una programación controlada por el sistema: Left no se ejecuta en segundo plano entre refrescos. El impacto en la batería es mínimo.
support.p_29: Sí: Left admite cuentas atrás conjuntas con amigos. Ambos necesitáis una cuenta de Left. Ve a la sección Friends, añade a tu amigo por nombre de usuario y luego crea un evento compartido juntos. Veréis los dos la misma cuenta atrás.
support.p_30: Los dos necesitáis tener iniciada la sesión en una cuenta de Left. Envía una solicitud de amistad por nombre de usuario desde la sección Friends y pídele que la acepte. Las cuentas atrás conjuntas y Shared Since estarán disponibles en cuanto seáis amigos.
